vocabulary.meaning: food that is thrown away instead of being eaten
examples: Households produce a large amount of food waste.
Reducing food waste can save money and resources.
We used the leftovers to make lunch the next day.
Freezing leftovers can reduce waste.

vocabulary.meaning: the date after which a product should no longer be used or eaten
examples: Always check the expiry date on fresh food.
Some people confuse the expiry date with the best-before date.

vocabulary.meaning: the date after which food may lose quality but may still be safe to eat
examples: The biscuits were still fine after the best-before date.
Understanding best-before dates can reduce unnecessary waste.

vocabulary.meaning: an amount of food served to one person
examples: Large portions can lead to more food waste.
I ordered a smaller portion because I was not very hungry.

vocabulary.meaning: decayed food and plant material used to improve soil
examples: Vegetable scraps can be turned into compost.
The restaurant composts some of its food waste.

vocabulary.meaning: to collect something and give it to different people or places
examples: Charities redistribute surplus food to families in need.
Supermarkets can redistribute food that would otherwise be wasted.

vocabulary.meaning: more of something than is needed
examples: The farm donated surplus vegetables.
A food surplus can still be useful if it is distributed quickly.

vocabulary.meaning: a place where waste is buried in the ground
examples: Food in landfill can produce greenhouse gases.
The city wants to send less organic waste to landfill.

vocabulary.meaning: able to continue without causing serious environmental damage
examples: Reducing waste makes the food system more sustainable.
Buying only what you need is a sustainable habit.
